question.text: An investor wants to consolidate two folios: Folio A (single holding by Priya) and Folio B (joint holding by Priya and Amit) — both with the same AMC. Can the RTA process this consolidation?

answer.text: No, because the holding pattern (single vs joint) is different — folios can only be consolidated if the holding pattern is identical
Yes, but only if Amit provides a No Objection Certificate
Yes, since Priya is common to both folios
Yes, but the consolidated folio will automatically become a joint holding

explanation.text: The Logic: Folios within the same AMC can be consolidated only when the holding pattern is identical — that is, the same set of holders, the same order of names, and the same mode of holding (Single, Joint, Anyone or Survivor, etc.). A single-holding folio held by Priya cannot be merged with a joint-holding folio held by Priya and Amit, because the holders and mode of holding differ. The RTA must therefore reject the consolidation request. The Trap: Having a common holder is not sufficient — every holder, the order of names, and the mode of holding must match. Two folios with the same two joint holders in different order may also not be consolidable. Note: The cited NISM Series II-B workbook pages discuss CAS consolidation by PAN/holding pattern and nomination rules, but the specific folio-consolidation rejection rule for single-versus-joint folios was not located in the pages checked. The framing above reflects general RTA industry practice rather than a workbook-page citation.
